### Assessment
Based on the image you shared, there is a strong possibility your maize plants are dealing with a fungal leaf disease. While the image model points toward gray leaf spot, our official verified records for maize leaf issues cover Northern leaf blight, also known as Turcicum leaf blight. You will want to look out for long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on your leaves, which can measure anywhere from 2.5 to 15 cm long. These spots can sometimes join together until large parts of your leaves look burnt. Remember, these treatments protect healthy plant tissue and slow down disease spread, but any leaves that are already dead or badly damaged will not turn green again. Please keep in mind that this image result is only an initial assessment. You should always double-check your fields in person before deciding to apply any chemical treatment.

It is very important to start early when you first notice these signs. If you decide to use a spray, make sure you get good leaf coverage so the medicine reaches all parts of the plant that still need protection. 

### How to Manage and Prevent Further Spread
To keep this fungus from taking over your field next season, try to use resistant maize hybrids whenever you can. You should also practice crop rotation and properly manage leftover crop residue, because the fungus loves to hide in infected maize stalks and leaves from previous harvests. Make a habit of scouting your fields both before and after tasseling, and only treat your crops when the actual risk and field conditions justify it.
